title: Health Surveillance Actions for Detecting  Tuberculosis and Human Immunodeficiency  Virusamong People Deprived of Liberty in Gaza Province, Southern Mozambique
content:
Introduction: Prisons in Mozambique are severely overcrowded, housing over twice their intended capacity. Furthermore, infectious disease surveillance, healthcare delivery and health education programmes remain poorly integrated with national public health strategies policies.
Objective: To describe healthcare and surveillance actions for the detection of Tuberculosis (TB) and HIV among prisoners in Mozambique.
Methods: A quantitative, cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in Gaza Province, Mozambique, across the prisons of the districts of Xai-Xai, Chongoene, and Mabalane. The study population comprised health professionals (HPs) and prison agents (PAs). Descriptive, univariate, and bivariate analyses were performed to evaluate infrastructure and diagnostic flow networks. A p-value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
Results: A total of 81 participants responded to the survey, representing a response rate of 81%. Of these, 64.2% (n = 52) were health professionals (HPs) and 35.8% (n = 29) were prison agents (PAs). The majority of respondents (92.5%, n = 75) reported the absence of an appropriate and adequately equipped area for sputum collection. Awareness of specialised TB and HIV treatment services was reported by 58% (n = 47) and 50.6% (n = 41) of participants, respectively. All participants (100%) indicated the absence of an established referral or transfer flowchart for people deprived of liberty (PDL) undergoing TB and/or HIV treatment, and no systematic entry screening for these diseases was reported.
Conclusion: The study underscored the need to improve environmental and safety conditions in areas designated for sputum collection, implement structured transfer protocols for people deprived of liberty (PDL) undergoing TB and HIV treatment, and establish systematic screening for infectious diseases upon entry into the prison system.
